results.finding: A viral-like prodrome (headache, fever, upper respiratory or gastrointestinal symptoms) precedes the neuropsychiatric syndrome in about 70% of patients.
results.source: Dalmau J et al. Lancet Neurol 2011;10:63-74

results.finding: Patients aged 45 or more had fewer teratomas; tumors, mostly carcinomas, were found in about a quarter.
Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included, after reasonable exclusion of other disorders.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

output.summary: Published evidence on SARS-CoV-2 and anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis consists of case reports and small series; cohort data describe an infectious-like prodrome in most patients and, after age 45, fewer teratomas and more carcinomas.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Give IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges) now, without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded, and repeat IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days, since three days of steroid gave only transient benefit.
Contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumor: repeat tumor screening, including pelvic imaging, during follow-up if the course is refractory or relapsing.

Treat the ongoing seizures by adding levetiracetam or lacosamide to valproate (level 68 mcg/mL, ammonia normal), and recheck the valproate level during acyclovir or plasma exchange; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.

Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for autonomic instability (heart rate to 125, blood pressure 100/60 to 160/100 mmHg, diaphoresis), recurrent seizures and dysphagia, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.
Keep her nil by mouth until a swallowing assessment, with nasogastric feeding and aspiration precautions.
Give empirical IV thiamine (200 mg three times daily) before glucose-containing fluids, given severe vomiting early in the illness, dysphagia with poor oral intake, encephalopathy and truncal ataxia.
Perform the lumbar puncture at least 12 hours after the last prophylactic enoxaparin dose and restart enoxaparin no sooner than 4 hours after it.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role here: the quadriparesis is upper motor neuron (brisk reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs) and is explained by the corticospinal tract lesions.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology; a four-week post-infectious illness with seizures, dyskinesias and dysautonomia is not a neurodegenerative presentation.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.diagnosis: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) or other viral encephalitis, including SARS-CoV-2
differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, enterovirus and SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative; MRI without temporal or insular involvement or hemorrhage; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: ADEM or MOG antibody-associated disease / NMOSD after COVID-19
differential.key_features: Serum MOG-IgG and aquaporin-4-IgG negative on cell-based assay; lesions are symmetric deep and tract-based rather than large multifocal demyelinating lesions; CSF anti-GluN1 explains the syndrome.

Severe vomiting early in the illness, dysphagia with poor intake, confusion and truncal ataxia fit, but there is no ophthalmoplegia or nystagmus and the MRI spares the medial thalami, mammillary bodies and periaqueductal gray; seizures, dyskinesias and CSF antibodies are not explained.
Ammonia 31 umol/L, valproate level 68 mcg/mL and liver tests normal; the encephalopathy preceded valproate.
Serum neuronal-surface panel (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX) and onconeural antibodies negative; no tumor on CT.

Four-week post-infectious course with CSF pleocytosis and oligoclonal bands; restricted diffusion is in the dentate nuclei and corticospinal tracts rather than the cortical ribbon or striatum; no periodic sharp-wave complexes.
Seizures, quadriparesis with Babinski signs, dyskinesias, dysautonomia, EEG and CSF abnormalities.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced psychosis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome
differential.key_features: No antipsychotic exposure; urine drug screen negative; CK only 245 U/L.

key_clinical_evidence: Four weeks after COVID-19, progressive behavioral change, mutism and disorganized speech, generalized and subclinical seizures, orolingual dyskinesias and dystonia, fluctuating responsiveness and autonomic instability: all six Graus 2016 groups, with quadriparesis, ataxia and urinary retention.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:1280) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:640 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows symmetric dentate, inferior cerebellar peduncle and corticospinal tract lesions with restricted diffusion; with negative MOG and aquaporin-4 antibodies and negative CSF viral PCRs (HSV, SARS-CoV-2) it excludes HSV encephalitis and does not establish a demyelinating syndrome.
EEG shows extreme delta brush and right temporal seizures with behavioral arrest; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumor; at 50 the tumor risk is lower and shifts toward carcinoma, so screening is repeated if the course is refractory.
Only transient benefit after three days of steroid: IVIG or plasma exchange is due now; earlier immunotherapy is associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses (SARS-CoV-2 and HSV negative here).
red_herrings.data_point: Confirmed COVID-19 (fever, cough, myalgia) about four weeks before the neurological decline; SARS-CoV-2 PCR still positive (Ct 32).
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a direct viral (SARS-CoV-2) encephalitis or COVID-related encephalopathy and delays antibody testing.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, upper motor neuron signs and CSF inflammation accompany the behavioral change and must be explained before a psychiatric diagnosis is considered.
red_herrings.data_point: Emotional lability, disorganized behavior and mutism in a previously healthy 50-year-old woman.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a psychiatric or functional explanation and delays the neurological work-up.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing instead of the neurological work-up.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward ADEM, MOG antibody disease or a toxic-metabolic leukoencephalopathy and away from antibody testing.

patient.history_present_illness: This 50-year-old previously healthy right-handed Caucasian woman is transferred to the emergency department from an outside rehabilitation facility for worsening neurological status. Her illness began approximately four weeks ago when she developed fever, cough, myalgia, and general malaise. She tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 by PCR and was admitted to a local hospital a week later after developing severe nausea, vomiting, and progressive weakness of all limbs. During that hospitalization, she became increasingly confused and exhibited disorganized behavior, including attempting to leave the ward, speaking incoherently, and displaying marked emotional lability with unprovoked crying and laughing. Notably, her oxygen saturation remained normal throughout and she showed no significant respiratory compromise. She received a course of treatment at the outside hospital including three daily pulses of intravenous methylprednisolone, sodium valproate for suspected seizure activity, enoxaparin for thromboprophylaxis, and esomeprazole. She was discharged home after brief improvement but continued to deteriorate. Ten days ago, she was transferred to a rehabilitation facility due to persistent emotional lability, progressive weakness affecting all four limbs, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, urinary retention, and worsening cognitive impairment. Valproate, enoxaparin and esomeprazole were continued at the rehabilitation facility, and her last enoxaparin dose was given 6 hours before arrival. At rehabilitation, her condition continued to decline. The physical therapy team noted she was unable to stand or walk independently and exhibited truncal ataxia. She developed new involuntary repetitive lip-smacking and jaw movements that were initially attributed to anxiety. Over the past 48 hours, her husband reports she has become nearly mute, is barely recognizable in her behavior, and has had two witnessed episodes of generalized body stiffening with rhythmic jerking of all extremities lasting one to two minutes each. She has also been noted to have episodes of profuse sweating, rapid heart rate, and blood pressure fluctuations. The patient has no prior psychiatric history, no history of autoimmune disease, no recent travel other than routine local activities before illness, and no illicit drug use.

neurological_exam.additional: Prominent orolingual dyskinesias with stereotyped lip-smacking, jaw clenching, and involuntary tongue movements. Episodes of autonomic instability observed during examination including transient tachycardia to 125 bpm, blood pressure fluctuations between 100/60 and 160/100 mmHg, and profuse diaphoresis. Urinary retention requiring indwelling catheter. Three brief episodes of behavioral arrest lasting 10-20 seconds each observed during the 30-minute encounter, concerning for subclinical seizures.
neurological_exam.coordination: Unable to reliably perform finger-to-nose or heel-to-shin testing due to encephalopathy. Truncal ataxia observed when patient briefly sits upright with assistance.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive, 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements intact without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact to light touch bilaterally. Mild left-sided lower facial weakness noted. Hearing grossly intact. Gag reflex present bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline with intermittent involuntary protrusion movements. Prominent orolingual dyskinesias with repetitive lip-smacking, jaw clenching, and tongue movements observed throughout examination.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Severely confused and disoriented to time, place, and person. Periods of marked agitation alternating with episodes of unresponsiveness lasting 20-40 seconds. Speech is severely dysarthric and disorganized with echolalia and perseveration. Unable to follow two-step commands. MMSE attempted but patient unable to cooperate; estimated score less than 10/30. Short-term memory profoundly impaired. Emotional lability with unprovoked crying episodes.

Strength difficult to assess reliably due to encephalopathy and inconsistent cooperation; appears globally reduced, approximately 3/5 in all four extremities when patient engages. Intermittent dystonic posturing of both hands observed. No focal asymmetry convincingly demonstrated.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+ bilaterally, triceps 3+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 3+ bilaterally, patellar 3+ bilaterally, Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Bilateral Babinski signs present (upgoing plantar responses).
neurological_exam.sensory: Decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the left face, left tongue, and left upper and lower extremities. Withdraws to pain symmetrically. Detailed sensory examination limited by encephalopathy.
